name: gaps
title: What HAL-FORMS Doesn't Carry Today
kicker: Beyond caching, what a replay loses
html:
What HAL-FORMS Doesn't Carry Today

GapWhat it costsAn extension could add
No integrity per templateThe kept script pins no form (here: 0 forms, 2 links); a replay can't tell a form changed under ithr:integrity per template
HTML input types onlyNo integer, no object or array; an object's shape comes from the goal's wordsa JSON Schema per template, by link
Fewer checks before sendingMore mistakes caught only by the serverthe same schema
No description of the actThe model chooses with lessdescription, a link to the ALPS descriptor

HAL-FORMS's spec allows extensions that add optional properties, which plain clients ignore. Not a commitment: HAL Schema Forms already carries all four, and is the more robust choice for replays with no model. HAL-FORMS stays the L0 on-ramp.
say: Everything in this release works in HAL-FORMS. What it doesn't carry today is the safety and precision layer. No integrity hash on a template, so the kept script pins no form, and a replay can't tell that a form changed under it. No real types, so an integer is just text and an object can't be described. Fewer checks before sending. No description of the act for the model. Could HAL-FORMS be extended to carry these? Yes: its spec lets anyone add optional properties, and plain clients ignore what they don't know. An integrity per template, a description, a schema by link would close each gap. We're not committing to that. HAL Schema Forms already carries all of it, and it's the more robust choice for a replay with no model.
